title: Call manifest normalizer and diagnostics playbook
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Design and deliver a canonical lightweight JSON manifest and a runtime normalizer that unifies function/tool calling payloads across SDK versions and model output shapes. Focus areas: a) a minimal, forward-compatible schema declaration for tool parameters, b) deterministic validation error taxonomy (retryable vs user errors), c) runtime marshalling rules and a compatibility shim that accepts legacy shapes and produces consistent diagnostics for SDKs and Console.
background: We have multiple incompatibilities observed in the field: older SDKs send positional arrays for some tool args, certain models emit loosely typed strings for numeric fields, and different runtimes produce different error messages. This ticket creates a single normalizer component in the runtime that: (1) consumes a canonical manifest attached to tool registrations, (2) applies coercion and guarded fallbacks, (3) emits structured diagnostics with stable error codes for observability and SDK mapping.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts canonical manifest and normalizes at least three legacy shapes (positional arrays, stringified numbers, nested single-key wrappers)
Validation error taxonomy implemented and documented with stable codes (ERR_PARAM_REQUIRED, ERR_PARAM_TYPE, ERR_PARAM_RANGE, ERR_COERCION_WARNING)
SDK mappings added: Node/Python map runtime error codes to user-facing messages and suggested fixes
Integration tests cover coercion, non-coercible rejections, and metric emission for validation errors
Rollout plan documented and feature-flag gated for canary customers
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chosen a minimal manifest shape inspired by OpenAPI 'schema' but reduced to primitives + enum + array with explicit 'coerce' flag
2026-03-12: Coercion default off for PII-sensitive fields; opt-in via manifest property 'allow_coercion'
2026-03-12: Error codes will be 5-character stable strings prefixed with 'RC' (runtime-call) to avoid collision with other systems
2026-03-13: Compatibility shim will be layered in runtime (pre-validate hook) rather than SDK-side to centralize telemetry
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Spike completed comparing manifest syntaxes (OpenAPI, JSON Schema, custom compact). Recommendation: custom compact format for lower runtime overhead.
2026-03-11: Prototype normalizer implemented (Go) that handles string->int coercion and positional->named mapping. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842
2026-03-12: Draft taxonomy and sample messages shared with SDK owners in #sdk-infra; comment from María Alvarez: prefer explicit suggestions in user errors
2026-03-13: Added metric hooks for validation.error.count and validation.coercion.count in prototype; initial dashboard created: https://app.datadog.com/dash/abc123/validation-signals
2026-03-14: Security raised question about coercion for encrypted fields; added 'sensitive' manifest attribute and default deny coercion for sensitive types
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and coercion rules covering 20 positive and negative cases
Property-based fuzz tests for model-emitted shapes to ensure safe rejections
End-to-end contract test: register a toy tool with manifest, call via legacy SDK payloads, assert normalized wire format reaches tool handler
Performance test: measure added parse time at 99th percentile under production retrace (target < 0.5ms per request)
Integration test verifying metrics (validation.error.count) increment on failures
rollout_plan: Canary rollout: 5% of traffic for internal Redwood tenants for 48 hours
Observe metrics and console error volume; if >3x baseline or SLO degradation, rollback
SDK release notes and migration guide published before 100% enablement
notes_for_reviewers: We intentionally avoid full JSON Schema to keep runtime parsing cheap; review whether this trade-off is acceptable for enterprise users who might expect richer constraints
Confirm semantics of 'allow_coercion' and 'sensitive' attributes with Security and Compliance
Verify error-code namespace doesn't conflict with Console alerting rules
follow_up_tasks: SDK owners to add humanized error mapping for new runtime codes
Add 'manifest lint' to Console tool registration flow
Post-release: collect prompt/eval failure examples and produce a short 'migration recipe' doc
original_author_notes: Aim for minimal cognitive overhead for tool authors: example-first manifests and a small set of coercion rules. Keep telemetry expressive enough to automate remediation hints in Console.
estimated_risks: Over-coercion could mask data errors and cause silent downstream failures
Performance cost of parsing manifests at high QPS if implemented naively
Enterprise customers may request full JSON Schema support, increasing scope
